findings.description: The bucket is explicitly annotated as public and no ACL, bucket policy restriction, or aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is configured, so public/anonymous read access to the objects it holds (including the customer master data object) is possible.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced SSE/KMS encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket produces no audit trail and unauthorised object reads would be undetectable.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably (including by an attacker destroying evidence).
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so data may be transmitted to and from the bucket over unencrypted HTTP.

A file named customer-master.xlsx is committed in the repository (resources/customer-master.xlsx) and uploaded to a bucket that is annotated as public and has no encryption, exposing potentially sensitive customer records both in version control and in the bucket. No kms_key_id or server_side_encryption is set on the object.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this financial-data bucket, leaving no audit trail of object access.
Versioning is absent while force_destroy is true, so objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten with no recovery path.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data publicly without a guardrail.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so there is no record of read or write access to this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guardrail is attached to prevent future public ACLs or policies on this bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data-science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest with no customer-managed key control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guardrail is attached to prevent future public ACLs or policies on this bucket.

The audit-log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no TLS-enforcing bucket policy; log data is security-sensitive and should be protected against accidental public exposure and cleartext transport.
